Work ONLY inside /opt/nxeon-wt-prison (a pre-created git worktree, branch `feature/freemc-prison`, off the Nxeon hosting platform's main repo). Do NOT touch /opt/nxeon or any other /opt/nxeon-wt-* directory — those are other people's/other agents' work happening concurrently. `node_modules` and `.env` in your worktree are symlinks to the main repo (normal) — but NEVER run `git add -A` there, it's a known hazard that can corrupt the main repo's real `node_modules` through the symlink. Only ever `git add` the exact file paths you changed.

This is a real production hosting business (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres). Free Minecraft hosting product; customers get a personal Minecraft server on a shared host (`freemc-host`, itzg/docker-minecraft-server images on Paper).

## Background — read this first, it's the whole playbook for this task

We just spent a long session fixing an identical-shaped bug in the "SkyBlock" game type. SkyBlock's plugin (IridiumSkyblock) was correctly installed, but its DEFAULT config had `islandCreateOnJoin: false`, `spawnOnIsland: false`, and an invalid `paster: "worldedit"` setting (WorldEdit isn't installed) — so a customer selecting SkyBlock just landed in plain default-generator terrain that looked exactly like vanilla Minecraft, with zero indication a skyblock plugin was even active. We root-caused every piece of this by SSHing into the real host and inspecting the plugin's actual config/database/logs directly — never guessing. The fix (in `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`, inside `recreateGameTypeContainer`, look for the block gated on `if (params.gameTypeKey === "skyblock")`) patches the plugin's config file via a `sed` command run right after the container's first boot, before the mode-properties restart, so it costs no extra restart cycle. Read that whole function (and the surrounding `waitForServerReady` helper) before you start — this is the exact pattern to follow for Prison.

## The task

The customer just reported: "i loaded up prison but this also looks like vanilla." A prior read-only investigation found:

- Prison's `FREEMC_GAME_TYPES` (or similarly-named constant) entry in `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts` installs a plugin via `SPIGET_RESOURCES: "1223"` (a SpigotMC resource, installed via itzg's spiget downloader) plus `luckperms,viaversion` via `MODRINTH_PROJECTS`.
- There is NO world generator override (confirmed: no `LEVEL_TYPE`/`GENERATOR_SETTINGS`/void-world anywhere for prison), no post-boot config patch (unlike SkyBlock), and no `setupNote` telling the customer they need to do anything themselves.
- Most Bukkit "Prison" plugins (mine/rank/economy genre) ship with ZERO pre-built mines — an admin normally has to define mine regions via in-game commands (often WorldEdit-dependent) before there's anything actually different from vanilla to mine.
- The same investigation flagged **parkour** and **missilewars** as likely having the identical gap (plugin installed, no actual arena/course setup, no setupNote) — worth a quick check while you're in there, same fix pattern if confirmed.

## What to do

1. **Identify exactly what SpigotMC resource 1223 is.** Use WebSearch/WebFetch on spigotmc.org (resource ID 1223) to find its name, its actual command set, and whether it ships any built-in default mine or requires manual mine creation. Don't guess — confirm from its actual documentation/description.

2. **Verify live against the real host**, the same way the SkyBlock bugs were root-caused — don't trust the plugin's docs alone, check what it actually does when running:
```ts
import { db } from "./lib/db"; // relative to /opt/nxeon-wt-prison
import { withServerSsh, exec } from "./lib/ssh-exec";
const host = await db.server.findFirst({ where: { hostname: "freemc-host" }, select: { id:true, rootPassword:true, rootPasswordEnc:true, sshPort:true, dedicatedIp:{select:{address:true}} } });
await withServerSsh(host!, async (conn) => {
  const r = await exec(conn, "docker logs <container> --tail 100", 10000);
  console.log(r.stdout, r.stderr);
});
```
You can boot a genuinely fresh, throwaway prison-type test container on `freemc-host` to inspect its plugin config/data directory and boot logs directly (`docker exec <container> ls /data/plugins/<PluginName>/`, `cat` its config files, check `docker logs` for warnings) — mirror exactly how the SkyBlock investigation copied `IridiumSkyblock.db` out via `docker cp` and inspected it with `python3 -c "import sqlite3; ..."`, and how it found the invalid `paster` setting from a boot-log warning. Do NOT touch the live, currently-in-use test container `mc-free-cmrztujaw0002hlazl58i3lsi` (that's a different, real in-use SkyBlock server — leave it alone). Create your own separate test container on the same host for this investigation, and clean it up (`docker rm -f`) when done unless told otherwise.

3. **Implement the fix**, matching whichever of these is actually true once you've confirmed it:
   - If the plugin needs an admin/console command to auto-create a default mine on first boot: add a post-boot patch block for `gameTypeKey === "prison"` in `recreateGameTypeContainer`, following the exact structural pattern of the SkyBlock block (runs after the first `waitForServerReady`, before `applyModeProperties`, so it doesn't add an extra restart cycle) — issue whatever RCON command(s) the plugin needs to create a starter mine automatically, so a customer selecting Prison gets an actual working mine with zero manual steps, same as SkyBlock now auto-creates an island.
   - If auto-creation genuinely isn't feasible (e.g. requires WorldEdit region-selection that can't be scripted), add an honest `setupNote` to the Prison entry — check `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts` for the `FreeMcPreset`/game-type type definition and look at how `towny` and `survivalgames` already use `setupNote` for a real precedent of the tone/format to match.
   - Apply the same finding to **parkour** and **missilewars** if you confirm they have the identical gap — same fix pattern (auto-setup if feasible, honest setupNote if not).

## Constraints — important

- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` inside `/opt/nxeon-wt-prison` before finishing.
- Commit with a clear message. Do NOT merge to main, do NOT touch staging, do NOT run deploy/promote scripts — a human handles integration and production deployment separately, on purpose.
- Report back: what resource 1223 actually is, what you found live on the test host, the fix you implemented (and for which game types), files touched, and confirm you committed on `feature/freemc-prison`.

622	  await sleep(3_000);

626	      return { ok: false, error: "Container exited before finishing startup." };
627	    }
628	    const logs = await exec(conn, `docker logs ${shellQuote(containerName)} --tail 200 2>&1`, 10_000);

Preparing the area ​ Before you can start setting up the area, you should make sure that it meets the following requirements: The parkour area is at least 15x15x15 blocks. (a larger area is highly recommended) The parkour area is mostly clear of other blocks (having it be completely empty of other blocks is recommended) (optional) a place the player will be teleported to when they fall. Otherwise, make sure they are not trapped if they fall. (optional) a place where the player can walk into to start parkour (a portal) Creating the area ​ The first step to start the creation process is the create and name the area. To do this, use the command /ajParkour setup create <name> . Example: /ajParkour setup create spawn will create an area named spawn . Setting the area ​ Next, you need to set the actual area of the parkour. To do this, you can use the commands /ajParkour setup pos1 and /ajParkour setup pos2 . These commands are similar to worldedit's //pos1 and //pos2 Speaking of worldedit, you can use worldedit instead of the pos1 and pos2 commands. To do this, select the area with worldedit, then use /ajParkour setup we to tell ajParkour to use that area. Setting the difficulty ​ Next, you need to set the difficulty of the area. To do this, you use the command /ajParkour setup difficulty <difficulty> . Here are the difficulties and how hard they are: Difficulty # of blocks per jump Easy 1 Medium 1-2 Hard 2-3 Expert 4-5 Balanced See below Balanced difficulty ​ The balanced difficulty will increase the difficulty as the player gets a higher score. Here is a table that shows what difficulty each score is at. Score Difficulty 0-9 Easy 10-29 Medium 30-69 Hard 70+ Expert This can be changed in jumps.yml (optional) Setting a fall position ​ If you would like the plugin to teleport the player somewhere when they fall (like near a start portal), you can set the fallpos. To set this, you stand where you would like the player to be teleported and type /ajParkour setup fallpos . Saving the area ​ First, you should double-check that you have set all of the required positions by typing /ajParkour setup info . If you see anything that is red, you will need to go back and set that. If you do not see any red in the info message, you can go ahead and save the area by typing /ajParkour setup save . With the first [installation](/RedstoneFuture/missilewars/wiki/Installation-Steps), all files are generated and fully loaded.

# 1. Lobby World Check

The arena files with the configuration and the template world area located in `/MissileWars/arenas/`. These files are fine so far and do not need to be adjusted for now.

The lobby configuration located in `/MissileWars/games/`. In the default game config `game1.yml` you only have to check if the `lobby.world` setting is pointing to a world it also exists on your server, at the beginning. Because the lobby - unlike the arena - is not created temporarily by the plugin. So, by default, you need a world "world" or you have to change the lobby-world setting here.

```yml
lobby:
  world: "world"
```

# 2. Checking your Updater-Block Setting

In the main configuration file `config.yml` located in `/MissileWars/` you see the `temp_block` setting-section for the [[Updater‐Block]]. If you want to use the default schematic files of this plugin located in the `/MissileWars/missiles/` folder, you should apply the following settings, as the Updater-Block is already included in the schematics files.

## Recommended Config for WorldEdit

> **Tip:** If you use WorldEdit, you can also completely deactivate the temporary Updater-Block after adjusting the schematic files. You can find the instructions [here](/RedstoneFuture/missilewars/wiki/Updater%E2%80%90Block#the-updater-block-in-your-schematic).

```yml
temp_block:
  enable: true
  material: NOTE_BLOCK
  remove_after_ticks: 4
  radius: 8
```

## Recommended Config for FastAsyncWorldEdit ("FAWE")

```yml
temp_block:
  enable: true
  material: NOTE_BLOCK
  remove_after_ticks: 0
  radius: 8
```

# 3. Generate a Game Sign

Find any place on your server and place a sign. Any sign materials can be used (Material-Tag: `#all_signs`).

The first line of the tag contains the keyword `[missilewars]` or `[mw]` (case-insensitive). The second line contains the name of the game: `game1` (case-sensitive).

![Screenshot](./pictures/Game-Sign.gif)

> **Note:** "Hanging Signs" are small and therefore offer less space for the text. When using this signs, shorten the `sign` lines and the `game_state` messages in the `messages.yml` and the `name` in the arena configuration, that the generated texts are not sometimes cut off.

(The positions of the generated MissileWars signs are saved in the `/MissileWars/data/signs.json` file.)

# 4. Prevent "Moved Wrongly" Messages

By default, SpigotMC spams a warning message "%player% moved wrongly!" in the console during the game. To prevent this, it's recommended to increase in the `spigot.yml` the `moved-wrongly-threshold` value from `0.0625` (= default) to `1.0625` or similar.

Info about SpigotMC configuration: https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/spigot-configuration

# 5. Game-Join

Finished! Now you and your test partner can right-click on the sign to go to the lobby. In the lobby, you can wait util the waiting time is done or as an Admin you can use the `/mw start` command.

You will be teleported to the arena and can play.

# The Game Concept behind MissileWars

In Minecraft MissileWars, players compete in a fast-paced, team-based game where the objective is to destroy the opposing team's portal using Missiles while defending your own.
